content: The cause is clear: in `formfield_for_manytomany()` the widget is assigned unconditionally, so a caller-supplied `widget` kwarg is overwritten — while `formfield_for_foreignkey()` guards its widget logic with `if 'widget' not in kwargs:`. Applying the same guard:
reasoning_content:
The cause: in `formfield_for_manytomany`, the widget is set unconditionally (no `if 'widget' not in kwargs` guard), unlike `formfield_for_foreignkey`. So a user-supplied `widget` kwarg gets overwritten.

Minimal fix: wrap the widget selection in `if 'widget' not in kwargs:`.

In `django/contrib/admin/options.py`, `BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_manytomany()` assigned `kwargs['widget']` unconditionally in its autocomplete/raw-id/filtered-select branches — so any `widget` a caller passed to the method was silently overwritten. Its sibling `formfield_for_foreignkey()` wraps the same kind of logic in `if 'widget' not in kwargs:`, which is why the override worked there but not for M2M fields.

    if db_field.name in autocomplete_fields:
